title: Optimistic Like Update
prompt: A React feed applies an optimistic like update before the server responds. Write a helper that returns a new post object with liked flipped and likeCount increased by 1 when becoming liked or decreased by 1 when becoming unliked.

explanation.beginner:
Example: optimisticLike({"id":"1","liked":false,"likeCount":10}) produces {"id":"1","liked":true,"likeCount":11}. The result must follow this precise rule: A React feed applies an optimistic like update before the server responds. Write a helper that returns a new post object with liked flipped and likeCount increased by 1 when becoming liked or decreased by 1 when becoming unliked. Work with one argument at a time and distinguish the values that select a branch from the values returned by that branch.

Compare “unlikes a liked post”: input [{"id":"1","liked":true,"likeCount":10}] produces {"id":"1","liked":false,"likeCount":9}. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.

Tempting mistake: Do not hard-code the first example: the unlikes a liked post case changes the input contract’s boundary or shape. Compare the actual outputs rather than only checking whether both are truthy.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.
